narration.full_text: Namaste students! Welcome to our quiz section on Control and Coordination. This is your chance to test your understanding of the nervous and endocrine systems, and how plants coordinate. Let's dive right in with our first question. What are three main functions of the nervous system? Think about how it interacts with our surroundings and body movements. The nervous system collects information from surroundings, controls and coordinates muscle movement, and helps us recognize smell, taste, vision, and hearing through our sense organs. Moving on to the next question. Draw the structure of a neuron and label the cell body and axon. Also, name the part of the neuron where information is acquired and through which it travels as an electrical impulse. Information is acquired at the dendrite tip and travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body, then along the axon to its end. Now for a question about protection. Brain and spinal cord are two vital organs. How is our body designed to protect them? The brain is protected by the cranium and cerebrospinal fluid acts as a shock absorber. The spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column. Let's tackle the final question. Define a receptor and state its location. Mention two receptors in the forebrain and their functions. How do nerve impulses travel in our body? Receptors are specialized nerve cell tips that receive information, located in sense organs. Gustatory receptors detect taste, and olfactory receptors detect smell. Nerve impulses travel as electrical signals, initiated by chemical reactions at dendrite tips, moving to the cell body, then along the axon, and across synapses via neurotransmitters. Great job, everyone! You've successfully tested your knowledge on control and coordination. Keep revising!

visual_beats.description: Quiz title: Test Your Knowledge: Control and Coordination
Question: Write three main functions of the nervous system.

Answer: (i) Collects information from the surroundings. (ii) Controls and co-ordinates the movement of muscles. (iii) Helps to recognise smell, taste, vision, hearing etc. with the help of sense organs.

Question: (a) Draw the structure of neuron and label cell body and axon. (b) Name the part of neuron: (i) Where the information is acquired. (ii) Through which information travels as an electrical impulse.

Answer: (b) (i) The information is acquired at the end of the dendrite tip of a nerve cell (ii) The information travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end.
Question: 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them?

Answer: Brain is located inside a bony box, named as cranium and a fluid is present in this balloon, known as cerebrospinal fluid which is a shock absorber. Spinal cord is placed in a vertebral column and back bone protects it.
Question: (i) Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions (ii) How do nerve impulses travel in our body?

Answer: (i) Receptors: Specialised tips of some nerve cells which receive information from the surroundings. Location: Sense organs. Gustatory receptor: Detect taste. Olfactory receptor: Detect smell.
Answer: (ii) Nerve impulses travel as electrical signals, initiated by chemical reactions at dendrite tips, moving to the cell body, then along the axon, and across synapses via neurotransmitters.
